findings.title: Self-route timestamps use the Node server clock rather than SQL now()
findings.detail: The self API routes stamp new Date().toISOString() (the Node server clock) instead of SQL now(). This is still server-authoritative — the client never supplies the time — so NFR §46 is satisfied and no change is required. If strict now() parity is desired later, drive the writes from a default now() column or an RPC.

findings.title: Service-role guard bypass is by design; ownership enforced in route code
findings.detail: requireUser/requirePermission return the service-role admin client, so auth.uid() is null in Postgres and the guard's service-role bypass branch skips the ownership/open-state checks for API writes. Ownership is enforced in the route handlers (.eq('staff_id', staff.id) + conditional .is('ended_at', null) updates), exactly as the design documents and as the existing self routes do; the DB guards still protect any user-token write. No action needed.
